Something most people are not aware of — as skeptics, we don’t just go the extra mile when sourcing our ingredients, whether seafood, meat, poultry, etc., we go the extra 10-1000+ miles… literally.

We do this so that we can source the highest-quality ingredients possible — grades of which exceed some Michelin-starred kitchens.

It’s expensive… very expensive… and we know most people may not even realize the quality of seafood of which they’re eating.

But we do it anyway, because we are proud of what we do, and our customers deserve nothing but the best.

-

With that said, we recently introduced our U10 SEARED SCALLOPS, with butternut squash purée and corn ribs, as part of our fall menu.

We hope you love it as much as we do.

Our December BOTM, A beautiful but sometimes difficult to read story, follows Cora, the protagonist, who is in a physically and mentally abusive marriage.  Cora sets off to register her new sons name, but grapples with naming him after her abusive husband. When the registrar asks her what she would like to call the child, she hesitates....

The story spans 35 years and three different name choices and three different versions of her sons life.

The novel explores the ripple effect on domestic abuse and family.

I found it to be a gut wrenching and powerful read.

Looking forward to unpacking this together DECEMBER 3OTH @corradoscucina 6pm !

Our annual coaches dinner (unfortunately missing a few guys) was a chance to slow down, share ideas, and make sure we’re all aligned as this program continues to grow. No distractions — just honest conversation, accountability, and a shared vision for what we’re building.

This group pours an incredible amount of time, energy, and care into our players. The trust, collaboration, and standards in that room are what separate good programs from great ones.

We’re proud of the foundation, thankful for the families who believe in us, and excited for what’s ahead. The work continues — and we wouldn’t want to go to battle with anyone else.

We rise together!  THANK YOU Casa Belverdere as always for everything!! #tkr

🇮🇹 la meravigliosa Casa Belvedere si trova sul punto più alto, chiamato Toadt Hill, del distretto di Staten Island, al numero 79 della Howard Avenue. Realizzata in stile neo rinascimentale, ospita un centro culturale italiano, che organizza mostre d’arte, proiezioni di film, notti d’opera, e tanto altro. Dal suo giardino, si gode anche di una meravigliosa vista del ponte di Verrazzano

🇺🇸 the wonderful Casa Belvedere is located on the highest point, called Toadt Hill, in the Staten Island borough, at 79 Howard Avenue. Built in a neo-Renaissance style, it houses an Italian cultural center, which organizes art exhibitions, film screenings, opera nights, and much more. From its garden, you can also enjoy a wonderful view of the Verrazzano bridge

Afsari’s approach to cooking is nothing short of artistic. Born in Rajshahi, the city of silk and mangoes, she brings a meticulous eye for beauty and vibrant flavors to every dish she creates. In light of the escalating genocide in Gaza, the recent continuing bloody attacks on Lebanon, and the abhorrent support for Netanyahu in our own government, we call on our fellow NYC residents from Queens, Brooklyn and beyond to join us as we hold a bridge vigil for Gaza in Bay Ridge. Bay Ridge is home to longstanding and legendary Irish and Palestinian neighborhoods, and we ask both communities, along with any other activists to stand together in solidarity. We call on the United States, the State Government of New York, and the European Union to end their support for Israel and to hold Netanyahu accountable for his unspeakable crimes.

We welcome and encourage flags from all over the world- help us show that our solidarity with Palestine is far reaching

We join comrades from around the world, from Ireland to NYC to the West Bank, who have demonstrated unwavering solidarity with the Palestinian people, in this action.  We draw on the courage of our ancestors and knowledge of our own history of genocide and oppression as we show our support at the same time as our friends and family in Ireland.

Please bring your friends, voices, flags (from around the world), and banners to this event.  We look forward to standing with you.

Bay Ridge’s first legal cannabis dispensary is set to open in November following a contentious application process that drew opposition from some residents and elected officials.

Kaya Bliss, located on Third Avenue between 84th and 85th streets, has a tentative opening date in early November, with a grand opening planned for the first week of December, according to owners Edgar Kleydman, a former financial planner and father of four, and Giorgio Matesi, a sanitation worker and father of one.

Kleydman and Matesi have been friends for 25 years and both grew up in southern Brooklyn. The pair have been eager to start a business together and say they are excited to make their “lifelong dream” a reality in their “old stomping ground.”

“Opening a business here is kind of like coming home to do something we love in our hometown,” Kleydman told Brooklyn Paper during a recent tour of the former Pilo Arts hair salon, which is currently under construction ahead of the opening.

In light of the escalating genocide in Gaza, the recent continuing bloody attacks on Lebanon, and the abhorrent support for Netanyahu in our own government, we call on our fellow NYC residents from Queens, Brooklyn and beyond to join us as we hold a bridge vigil for Gaza in Bay Ridge. Bay Ridge is home to longstanding and legendary Irish and Palestinian neighborhoods, and we ask both communities, along with any other activists to stand together in solidarity. We call on the United States, the State Government of New York, and the European Union to end their support for Israel and to hold Netanyahu accountable for his unspeakable crimes.

We welcome and encourage flags from all over the world- help us show that our solidarity with Palestine is far reaching

We join comrades from around the world, from Ireland to NYC to the West Bank, who have demonstrated unwavering solidarity with the Palestinian people, in this action.  We draw on the courage of our ancestors and knowledge of our own history of genocide and oppression as we show our support at the same time as our friends and family in Ireland.

Please bring your friends, voices, flags (from around the world), and banners to this event.  We look forward to standing with you.

W mojej nowej książce będę starała się Wam pokazać również mniej znane oblicze Nowego Jorku, niepokazywane w setkach filmów. Wspominam o miejscach odkrytych przypadkiem, które mimo swojej wyjątkowości nie miały szans trafić do przewodników.

Jednym z nich jest “domek z piernika”, the Gingerbread house, stworzony na początku XX wieku w stylu “ruchu sztuki i rzemiosła” (ang. Arts and Crafts), inspirowany twórczością Johna Ruskina i Williama Morrisa. 

W zeszłym roku ta wyjątkowa posiadłość wpisana na listę New York City landmarks znowu trafiła na rynek, jej cena wywoławcza to 8.75 mln dolarów - oferta nawet okazyjna, biorąc pod uwagę nie tylko sam dom, ale również ogromny teren, na którym został zbudowany. Jeśli ktoś z Was się skusi, proszę mnie zaprosić! Z chęcią obejrzę w środku i posiedzę w basenie (tak! jest basen!)

Contemporary Flea started as an idea to gather the most creative people I know in design, arts and vintage. Some said no, some said maybe next time and a few said yes. For those who said yes, thank you for your trust.

Contemporary Flea is half a year old, so far heres what we’ve done:
•Inaugural three day market in June in @manacontemporary 
•Are We Home Yet? October Weekend Market @harborsidejc 
•Cars (and Art) and Coffee with @porschestimmung 
•Friendsgiving Bake Sale in collab w/ @now__serving c/o @likelysong 
•Launched “The Conversation Pit” by Sydney Gore @cozy.spice 
•Collab with Design Barbiana @designbarbiana on Contemporary Flea Sticker Pack (Design your own space)
•Collab with CycyMymy @cycymymydesign on a projection install
•Gallery Night w/ soundbath DJ set by @buddhabanji 
•showcase 100+ artists and designers
•host 50+ creative business as vendors
•gather 30+ food artists, bakers and drinks brand
•welcome 5000+ people across multiple events
•raise money and food donations for a local nonprofit

On December 5,6,7 we’re doing Contemporary Flea: The Holiday Edit
Hosting 50+ dealers in furniture, fashion, home goods alongside artists and designers.

Thanks to everyone who keeps on saying yes. 
See you at the ©️FLEA!

Dec 6 Saturday - explore the space and splurge on unique giftables. Panels featuring fresh voices in design will be lead by Sydney Gore. Linger by the cafe where food and drinks are available from local notable spots.

Thank you Tim for your dedication to helping others, your passion to save lives and for supporting the mission of the Overdose Response Network within the Clinton Foundation!

So much changes in a year- Happy one year to The Jersey City Cabaret. I’m honored to be a part of such a collaborative effort that’s brought a welcoming space for play. Thankful for the revolving door of artists that have come through this past year with ambitious hearts and open minds. Thankful for @threepeasproductions for curating and capturing moment to moment of our evolution. Hannah, Zach and Lauren have built this cabaret from the ground up and provided Jersey city with a new hub for creation and inclusivity, I will forever be grateful. Thank you to Isaac, our accompanist, for always giving our singers the most solid foundation. You’re a talent and a joy to work with each month and I always trust that you’ll keep us in the right space and time. 
Thank you Michael, for believing in me when I bought my first bass, with my last dollars, and said “hey man… I don’t know what the hell I’m doing.” You’ve taught me so much these past two years but mostly it was your confidence in me that lights a fire under my ass to keep challenging myself. Thank you for playing with me and indulging my chaos personally, and musically. 
Thank you Timothy, my love, for always being there to see me. You shine a light in the crowd and fill me with so much love and support. Thank you for always giving me the space and time to focus and create, thank you for your endless adoration and motivation for me and my music. I get knocked down and you pick me right back up again. 

It may not seem like much, but when I first started playing I didn’t think I’d be able to remember where the notes are on my fret board (don’t quiz me) let alone sing and play.

Here’s to support systems, open doors and the never ending challenge of just being. 

Happy thanksgiving 🍁

I’ve learned a lot about toners, color theory, and placement…
But what’s really stuck with me?
The human stuff. The hard stuff. The stuff no one tells you about when you hold your first pair of scissors. 

Here are 5 things I’ve learned in this beautiful, chaotic, healing, humbling industry:

⸻

1. You’re not just doing hair.

You’re holding someone during their breakup. Their job change. Their pregnancy. Their grief. People sit in your chair and show up raw—and you get the honor of helping them feel like themselves again. That’s not “just hair.”

⸻

2. The client isn’t always right—but they are always human.

Boundaries matter. Communication matters. Grace matters. And learning how to stand your ground with kindness is one of the most valuable skills in this job.

⸻

3. You can’t pour from an empty color bowl.

Burnout is real. Rest is productive. Your creativity needs recovery time. If you’re showing up exhausted every day, your work—and your joy—will suffer.

⸻

4. People remember how you made them feel more than how their layers flipped.

You could nail the formula, but if they didn’t feel seen, safe, or listened to? They’ll go elsewhere. This is a people-first business, and the hair is the cherry on top.

⸻

5. Your dream clients will find you when you show up as you.

Authenticity beats perfection. Every time. Stop trying to fit the “cool stylist” mold. Be your weird, wonderful, real self—and the right clients will find you. And stay.

⸻

If you’re in the industry too: What’s something you learned that changed how you show up behind the chair?👇
